solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Followers succeeded people on the radio

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
radio presenters and guests are talkers, people who talk on air

explanation.surface: Some radio personalities have been replaced by the presenters who came after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalkers are people who follow someone obsessively, so they are followers in a sinister sense.

clue.text: Very difficult to find mark on box, having wasted hours

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: something wasted is lost or thrown away, so the letter for hours drops out of the box word

parts.note: a chest is a large box for storage

explanation.surface: A mark on a box is hard to spot after hours of searching have been wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having wasted' removes H from CHEST, leaving CEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of scarce describes what is rarest, hardest of all to come by or locate.

clue.text: Count on good support for partner during The Four Seasons

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece holds up the upper one, so the count part sits beneath and supports the partner word

parts.note: an ally is a partner or associate
an earl is the British rank equivalent to a continental count
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nobleman relies on good backing for his companion while attending a performance of Vivaldi's The Four Seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' looks like a phrase meaning rely on, but Count is the nobleman EARL and on is just ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting through all four seasons means continuing for the whole twelve months, throughout the year.

clue.text: 70s figure opening for Kraftwerk belts out a few numbers

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from the band name

parts.note: someone who belts out songs is a singer, so the phrase reads as 'is singer'

explanation.surface: An act supporting the German electronic band Kraftwerk sings loudly through a short set.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Kissinger was US Secretary of State in the 1970s; the definition is loose, as the blog noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Kissinger was a prominent American statesman of the Nixon and Ford era, a key figure of that decade.

clue.text: Hold a grudge, having lost new boot again

indicators.note: losing a letter means it is dropped from the word for holding a grudge

parts.note: to resent something is to hold a grudge about it

explanation.surface: Someone stays bitter after their new boots went missing again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' is a computing verb here, not footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To reboot a computer is to restart it, returning it to its initial state, which is what resetting it does.

clue.text: Complete, our lunkhead

parts.note: to do a task is to complete it
something that is ours belongs to us, so it is 'of us'

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a job is finished while calling a member of their own group a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal American insults for a stupid, clumsy person, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Stops controlling this publication

definitions.meaning: an ... stops are the knobs that control which pipes sound
a newspaper or magazine serving as the mouthpiece of a group is called its house ...

explanation.surface: Someone halts the running of a magazine they control.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard instrument is governed by its stops, and a party newspaper is its official mouthpiece periodical.

clue.text: Cultivated US officer carrying gun?

indicators.note: the officer holds the weapon, so the gun word sits inside the officer word

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent or officer
an arm is a weapon, such as a gun

explanation.surface: A sophisticated American policeman is asked whether he is armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' suggests refined manners but is the farming sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that has been farmed has been tilled and planted, that is, cultivated for crops.

clue.text: Heard singer give out

indicators.note: something heard is spoken aloud, so the singer's name is matched by its sound

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer, whose name is pronounced like a word for a portion

explanation.surface: A listener caught a vocalist announcing something.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger felt the two do not rhyme in every accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out portions among people is to distribute or apportion them, the verb sense.

clue.text: A lot of body parts make a lot of effort

parts.note: many means a lot of
ears are parts of the body

explanation.surface: Lots of limbs and organs manage to put in a lot of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid entry is the hyphenated unit of labour; split differently, its letters spell a phrase for many body parts. 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-year is a unit of work done by one person in a year, so many of them means great labour.

clue.text: Very close to girl collecting English books

parts.note: to be at a place is to be right by it

indicators.note: the girl gathers the letter in, so it sits inside the girl word

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone stands right next to a young woman who is gathering English books.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plural noun 'books', at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlases are bound volumes of maps, so they are a kind of book.

clue.text: Country song about leg getting broken

indicators.note: the song wraps around the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: a broken limb is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballad tells the story of someone breaking their leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting broken' scrambles the limb before 'about' wraps the opera song round it; 'Country' at the start is the definition, not the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Science film covers first sign of rot in fruit

indicators.note: to cover for someone is to stand in for them, so the film takes the place of a letter

parts.note: a cherry is a fruit

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: A science documentary shows the first trace of decay appearing in fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' means stands in for, as one actor covers for another, not wraps: the film word takes the place of the first R only.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry is the branch of science dealing with substances and their reactions.

clue.text: Something to hang with energy returning shortly before

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: soon means a short time before something
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone's energy comes back just before they need it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns SOON into NOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope used to execute someone by hanging, so it is a tool to hang with.

clue.text: What planets do is burn to the ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: What planets do is burn to the ground in some cosmic catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' signals the rearrangement of IS BURN TO THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets travel in elliptical paths around their star, circling it continuously.

clue.text: Be dismissive of quiet game by leaving

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: the word for 'by' departs, so those letters are taken from the game

parts.note: rugby is a ball game
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a quiet game while walking away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug off something is to treat it as unimportant, dismissing it with a lift of the shoulders.

clue.text: Excellent! Former BBC man is coming back in to finish rant

indicators.note: these letters go inside the word for finishing

parts.note: to die is to come to an end, to finish
A, the top grade, means excellent

indicators.note: coming back means the name is read in reverse

parts.note: John Birt was Director-General of the BBC in the 1990s

explanation.surface: Someone cheers as an ex-BBC boss returns, then finishes with a tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns BIRT into TRIB; A plus TRIB goes 'in' DIE. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a rant.

clue.text: Learned fellow has a prayer for motor sport

parts.note: Dr, doctor, is the title of a learned person
grace is a prayer said before a meal

explanation.surface: An academic offers a prayer before a car race.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a sprint between two cars on a straight track, a form of motor racing.

clue.text: Resolve to out Teddy?

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to expose a person named Teddy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Teddy as one example: Theodore Roosevelt, whose nickname gave the teddy bear its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Roosevelt, the US president, was popularly known by the nickname Teddy.

clue.text: Make longer right turn after quiet hill-climbing

indicators.note: the right and turn pieces follow the quiet and hill pieces

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: in a down answer a climbing word reads upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: A driver takes a long right turn after a quiet climb up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns TOR into ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to draw it out or prolong it in time.

clue.text: Subservient people's party creating a storm

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: creating means forming something new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A group of meek people throws a party that causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' turns A STORM into ORMATS; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a person who lets others walk all over them, a submissive type.

clue.text: Draw naked swimmer

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a lottery is a draw for prizes

explanation.surface: An artist is told to sketch a nude bather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like the verb to sketch but is a prize draw.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is an aquatic mammal, a creature that swims well.

clue.text: Saw red journalist on rotten paper

indicators.note: the journalist piece follows on after the paper piece

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist lost their temper on seeing a terrible newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious, the same as being in a rage.

clue.text: Poles embracing American ways

indicators.note: the poles hug the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: rods are poles

explanation.surface: Polish people hugging an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but means sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are routes for travel, so they are ways in the sense of thoroughfares.

clue.text: Thick studies finally complete

parts.note: dens are studies, private rooms for work

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A dim student's studies are at last finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone slow-witted, or something closely packed, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Possibly report disturbance involving meat

indicators.note: the disturbance wraps around the other word, involving it

parts.note: a riot is a public disturbance
flesh is meat

explanation.surface: A news report tells of a riot breaking out over meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' means a bang, not a news story; 'Possibly' shows the answer is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, and the crack of a gun firing is one example.

clue.text: Women in line of battle mostly look unhappy

indicators.note: the women's letter goes inside the other piece
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: the front is the line where armies meet

explanation.surface: Women serving on the front line usually look miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts FRONT to FRON.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to wrinkle the brow in displeasure, showing unhappiness on the face.

clue.text: Annual battle in the Crimea may return

parts.note: the Battle of the Alma, 1854, was the first major battle of the Crimean War

indicators.note: returning means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: can and may both express permission

explanation.surface: A yearly anniversary of a Crimean War battle may come round again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annual' is a noun here: a yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a book published every year, a yearly reference volume.

clue.text: See 7
A lot of water around in buffalo pens earlier

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: There was a lot of water around the buffalo enclosures before.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea is the wide expanse of ocean away from land, water all around.

clue.text: Second snake further down

parts.note: an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: A second snake lies lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' means depressed, not lower.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down means being low in spirits, so more down is more unhappy.

clue.text: Bee, possibly short of energy, keeps egg back, having a gut feeling

indicators.note: the shortened word keeps the other piece inside it
short of means lacking, so the energy letter is removed

parts.note: a bee is one example of an insect
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A bee low on energy guards its egg, sensing danger instinctively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes E from INSECT to make INSCT; 'back' turns NIT into TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is innate knowledge acted on without reasoning, which is what a hunch or intuition is.
